# US Dictionary

> > A comprehensive reference for American English idioms, phrases, and expressions with detailed etymological origins and historical context.

US Dictionary provides in-depth explorations of English idioms and phrases, tracing their origins from classical sources like Old English, Latin texts, and literary works by authors such as H.G. Wells, Ernest Hemingway, and Robert Louis Stevenson. Each entry includes definitions, meanings, historical usage examples, and cultural context spanning from ancient Babylonian and Egyptian influences through modern American English.

## Key Topics

- Idiom definitions and meanings
- Etymology and phrase origins
- Figurative language in English
- Old English linguistic roots
- Historical literary references (H.G. Wells, Hemingway, Stevenson)
- Latin language influences
- 19th-century publications (Cassell's Family Magazine, Boston Traveller)
- American English expressions
- Social behavior and personality descriptors
- Cultural and historical context
- Non-verbal communication idioms
- Gratitude and courtesy phrases
- Time-related expressions
- Metaphorical language patterns

## Popular Idioms & Common Expressions

- [Jump on The Bandwagon: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/jump-on-the-bandwagon): Bandwagon idiom origins tied to Theodore Roosevelt & Spanish-American War
- [What Goes Around Comes Around: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/what-goes-around-comes-around): Karma idiom: biblical roots in Galatians 6:7 & Donald Goines usage
- [To Each His Own: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/to-each-his-own): Latin expression via John Dryden: tolerance & individual preference idiom
- [Food For Thought: Definition, Meaning, and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/food-for-thought): Figurative phrase origins in Boston Traveller & Literary News
- [Shiver Me Timbers: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/shiver-me-timbers): Pirate slang from Robert Louis Stevenson's Treasure Island nautical terms
- [Social Butterfly: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/social-butterfly): Social butterfly idiom: 200+ year history of personality descriptor

## Emotional & Relational Expressions

- [Have My Heart In It: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/have-my-heart-in-it): Emotional commitment phrase: figurative heart expression meanings
- [Long For: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/long-for): Old English yearning phrase traced to King James Bible Psalms
- [Kindred Soul: Definition, Meaning, And Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/kindred-soul): Spiritual connection phrase from Lady Morgan's Old English etymology
- [Bat Her Eyelashes: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/bat-her-eyelashes): Flirtation gesture: non-verbal communication & persuasion tactic history
- [Cutie Pie: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/cutie-pie): Term of endearment: affectionate language from Motion Picture era

## Gratitude & Courtesy Phrases

- [You Are More Than Welcome: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/you-are-more-than-welcome): Gratitude phrase evolution from Cassell's Family Magazine era
- [Thanks for Checking Up on Me: Definition, Meaning, How to Reply](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/thanks-for-checking-up-on-me): Gratitude expression traced to Hemingway's letters with reply guidance
- [Thanks Heaps: Definition, Meaning, and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/thanks-heaps): Australian/NZ slang: informal gratitude expression from Australasian English
- [Welcome Back: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/welcome-back): Greeting phrase etymology from Cervantes' Don Quixote & Old English

## Character & Resilience Idioms

- [Having a Broad Back: Definition, Meaning, and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/having-a-broad-back): Idiom definition: resilience metaphor traced to H.G. Wells' works

## Time & Duration Expressions

- [Dusk Till Dawn: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/dusk-till-dawn): Time phrase traced to John Milton's Paradise Lost literary reference
- [A Quarter To One: Definition, Meaning and Origin](https://usdictionary.com/idioms/a-quarter-to-one): Time expression history from Egyptian & Babylonian clock terminology
